behaviorEvidence: Two arbitrary applications and a native Workflow execute for a member without a plan review or publication review
Member publication and cross-author revision preserve exact old plan and material pins
Members cannot archive or withdraw public definitions; inactive bodies and review history remain stored
Own draft is visible after reload, another owner's draft and secret bindings are not readable
Legacy pending, denied, approved and UNKNOWN plans remain unchanged and never dispatch after policy migration
Same request retains one task/native job; two independent workers produce one original project-create effect
Native hazardous-tool confirmation remains separate; project-create exact consent and connection expiry are rechecked before admission
UNKNOWN workflow operations are only reconciled against original identity; cancel retains resources until positive original-stop evidence
Current disabled/revoked identity and expected-owner mismatches still deny operations
Task UI does not request or poll administrator reviews; historical reviews remain read-only
integrationRemaining: A-owned Settings/main assembly must select and accept member-self-service defaults and new policy revisions
A-owned App/navigation must expose application and material management to members
A application extraction must retain the personal-command execution guard, inject only historical research review summaries, and explicitly bind the existing research resource effect
limitations: No actual paid/live provider request or deployed environment was exercised
Historical explicitly selected policy fixtures remain for compatibility; they are not the new product default
Changing Settings, source extraction or shared navigation requires integrated verification on A's branch
